task_instruction: Rewrite each active sentence in the passive voice.
paragraphs: A science museum is preparing an exhibit about the female reproductive system. The education team reviews how the organs work. {{red:The ovaries release an egg during ovulation in many menstrual cycles.}} {{mask_1}} {{red:The body produces estrogen and progesterone in the ovaries.}} {{mask_2}} {{red:Researchers identified the influence of hormonal signals on the uterine lining in early studies.}} {{mask_3}} {{red:Clinicians are using ultrasound to examine the uterus during the demonstration.}} {{mask_4}}

The next display explains how the cycle is regulated. {{red:The pituitary gland releases hormones that affect ovarian activity.}} {{mask_5}} {{red:Scientists have studied changes in the uterine lining throughout the menstrual cycle.}} {{mask_6}} {{red:Laboratory staff were examining tissue samples when the curator arrived.}} {{mask_7}} {{red:The museum will present the new exhibit to local schools next month.}} {{mask_8}}

A medical educator checks the wording for accuracy and clarity. {{red:The guide describes the ovaries, uterine tubes, uterus, cervix, and vagina.}} {{mask_9}} {{red:Teachers explain the difference between menstruation and ovulation in the workshop.}} {{mask_10}} {{red:Hormonal changes can affect the thickness of the uterine lining.}} {{mask_11}} {{red:The team has not included personal medical advice in the exhibit.}} {{mask_12}}

The exhibit also describes fertilization and early development in general terms. {{red:Fimbriae guide a released egg toward a uterine tube.}} {{mask_13}} {{red:Tiny cilia and muscular contractions move the egg through the uterine tube.}} {{mask_14}} {{red:A fertilized egg may reach the uterus several days later.}} {{mask_15}} {{red:Clinicians use medical history and examination results to assess reproductive health.}} {{mask_16}}

Before opening day, the museum team reviews the displays with health educators. {{red:The designers are adding a diagram of the menstrual cycle this week.}} {{mask_17}} {{red:The curator had checked every scientific caption before the exhibit was installed.}} {{mask_18}} {{red:Researchers will update the information when new evidence becomes available.}} {{mask_19}} {{red:Public health teams should provide people with clear and reliable reproductive health information.}} {{mask_20}} The exhibit encourages visitors to discuss personal health questions with qualified clinicians.
